prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1315; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reports a sideswipe collision while changing lanes on a multi-lane roadway. Insured vehicle contacted the claimant's vehicle at the rear quarter panel. Claimant states they were in the adjacent lane and the other vehicle moved over without signaling. Photos of both vehicles requested. Police report number pending from the responding agency.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant reports neck and left shoulder pain beginning the evening of the collision and has been seen at an urgent care clinic. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and says they have not yet spoken with anyone about a settlement. Requested copies of all medical records and bills and explained the process for submitting them.

Entry 3: Recorded a recorded statement from the insured. Insured states they checked their mirrors and believed the lane was clear, but acknowledges the contact occurred as they moved left. Insured reports no injuries to themselves. Dashcam footage from the insured vehicle was requested and is expected to be provided within the week.

Entry 4: Reviewed the photos submitted by the claimant. Damage is visible along the rear passenger door and quarter panel of the claimant vehicle, with paint transfer on the insured vehicle's front right fender. Independent appraisal assigned for the claimant vehicle. Claimant has been given a rental vehicle authorization pending the repair estimate.

Entry 5: Claimant advised that the shoulder injury claim will be evaluated once the treating provider's records and an MRI report, if ordered, are received. Claimant asked about the timeline. Explained that the file will remain open pending medical documentation and that the claimant may contact the adjuster directly with questions. Follow-up call scheduled for later this week.
